## Background
The Home Owners’ Loan Corporation (HOLC) ranked houses by color, which led to the term "redlining". This is the basis of the social injustices to individuals living in these areas.

## Data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tmap)
library(here)
library(stars)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
```

```{r}
# HOLC redlining
holcgrade <- st_read(here('data','mapping-inequality','mapping-inequality-los-angeles.json')) |> 
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

# Environmental screening and mapping
ejscreen <- st_read(here('data','ejscreen','EJSCREEN_2023_BG_StatePct_with_AS_CNMI_GU_VI.gdb')) |> 
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

# bike and pedestrian crash reports
crashes <- read_csv(here('data','SWITRS_LA','crashes.csv')) |> 
  drop_na(POINT_X, POINT_Y) |> 
  st_as_sf(coords = c('POINT_X','POINT_Y'), crs = 4326)
```

```{r}
# Check coordinat systems
st_crs(ejscreen) # WGS84
st_crs(holcgrade) # WGS84
st_crs(crashes) # NA

st_crs(ejscreen) == st_crs(holcgrade) # TRUE
```

## Part 1: Legacy of redlining in current environmental (in)justice

Exploring the historical redlining in Los Angeles and its legacy on present-day environmental justice.

```{r}
# Map of historical redlining neighbourhoods in LA
losangeles <- ejscreen |> 
  filter(STATE_NAME == 'California', CNTY_NAME == 'Los Angeles County')

tm_shape(losangeles, bbox = c(-118.7, 33.65, -117.65, 34.35)) +
  tm_polygons(fill = 'white',
              lwd = 1) +
tm_shape(holcgrade) +
  tm_polygons(fill = 'grade',
             fill.legend = tm_legend(title = 'HOLC Grades',
                                    position = tm_pos_out("right"))) + # TODO: assign colors to the grades
tm_title(text = 'Los Angeles HOLC Neighborhoods') +
tm_graticules() +
tm_scalebar() +
tm_compass()
```

Summarize the data by percent of census block group by HOLC grade.

```{r}
# Join HOLC and LA spatially
holcgrade  <- st_make_valid(holcgrade)
losangeles <- st_make_valid(losangeles)

laholc <- st_join(holcgrade, losangeles, join = st_intersects) |> # st intersects??
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  select(ID, grade, LOWINCPCT, P_PM25, P_LIFEEXPPCT)
glimpse(laholc)
```

```{r}
# Summarize by census block group by HOLC grade
census_block_holc <- laholc |> 
  group_by(grade) |> 
  summarize(count = n()) |> 
  mutate(perc_census = count/sum(count)*100)
census_block_holc
```

Create visualizations

```{r}
conditions <- laholc |> 
  group_by(grade) |> 
  summarise(mean_low_pct = mean(LOWINCPCT, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_pm25 = mean(P_PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_lifeexp = mean(P_LIFEEXPPCT, na.rm = TRUE))
conditions
```

```{r}
# make color palette for the entire doc

plot1 <- ggplot(
  data = conditions,
  mapping = aes(
    x = mean_low_pct,
    y = mean_lifeexp,
    color = grade
  )
) + geom_point(size = 7) +
  xlab('Mean % Low Income') +
  ylab('Mean Percentile for Low Life Expectancy') +
  labs(color = 'HOLC Grade')

plot2 <- ggplot(
  data = conditions,
  mapping = aes(
    x = mean_pm25,
    y = mean_lifeexp,
    color = grade
  )
) + geom_point(size = 7) +
  xlab('Mean Percentitle for PM 2.5') +
  ylab('Mean Percentile for Low Life Expectancy') +
  labs(color = 'HOLC Grade')

plot <- plot1 + plot2
plot + plot_annotation(
  title = 'Mean Life Expectancy across HOLC Grades'
)
```

Based on the plot above, there is a strong pattern between HOLC grade and low life expectancy. As percent low income and PM 2.5 concentrations increase, low life expectancy increases as well. The grade with the highest values in all 3 categories is rank D, and vice versa for rank A. This means that redlining grades tend to have low life expectancy, high percent low income, and high percentile for PM 2.5 as compared to A grade.

## Part 2: Legacy of redlining in pedstrian and bike accidents

Explore the legacy of historical redlining in Los Angeles and pedestrian and bike crashes/fatalities.

Create a figure that summarizes the percent of observations within redlined neighbourhoods within each HOLC grade.

```{r}
# come back to this
crash_holc <- st_join(crashes, holcgrade, join = st_intersects) |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  select('grade','PEDESTRIAN_ACCIDENT','BICYCLE_ACCIDENT') |> 
  group_by(grade) |> 
  summarize(ped_accidents = n(), bike_accidents = n()) |> 
  mutate(perc_ped_acc = ped_accidents/sum(ped_accidents) * 100, 
         perc_bike_acc = bike_accidents/sum(bike_accidents) * 100)
crash_holc
```

```{r}
ggplot(crash_holc,
      aes())
```

```{r}
tm_shape(losangeles, bbox = c(-118.7, 33.65, -117.65, 34.35)) +
  tm_polygons(fill = 'white',
              lwd = 1) +
tm_shape(holcgrade) +
  tm_polygons(fill = 'grade',
             fill.legend = tm_legend(title = 'HOLC Grades',
                                    position = tm_pos_out("right"))) + # TODO: assign colors to the grades
tm_shape(crash_holc) +
  tm_dots() +
tm_title(text = 'Los Angeles HOLC Neighborhoods') +
tm_graticules() +
tm_scalebar() +
tm_compass()
```
